newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt police arrest 35 in latest farmer unrest.
newsitem.headline: Egypt police arrest 35 in latest farmer unrest.

text.p: Egyptian police arrested 35 farmers south of Cairo on Thursday in the latest outbreak of unrest over an agricultural land law which takes effect in October.

The Land Centre for Human Rights, an independent monitoring group, said the farmers were among a crowd of about 2,000 demonstrating outside the agricultural cooperative in the town of Gerza, 70 km (45 miles) from the capital.

The agricultural cooperatives have borne the brunt of peasant outrage at the law, which deregulates the market in farmland and deprives farmers of an automatic right to pass rented property on to their descendants.

Many tenant farmers think that as soon as the law takes effect the landlords will evict them and turn the land over to capital-intensive agrobusinesses. The government has promised to offer evicted farmers alternatives in reclaimed areas.

A spokesman for the Land Centre said the farmers at Gerza were angry that the agricultural cooperative was trying to register their land in the name of the landlord, abandoning the old practice of using the tenant's name.
"The police clashed with them and arrested 35," he added.
On Wednesday demonstrators set fire to an agricultural cooperative near the Nile Delta town of Mahalla el-Kubra, 120 km (75 miles) north of Cairo. About 150 people were arrested.
Three people were killed and dozens of demonstrators arrested in southern Egypt on Tuesday when police broke up a riot by farmers to protest the law, the Interior Ministry and security sources said.
President Hosni Mubarak said on Tuesday that the government had solved 90 percent of the problems raised by the law in the five years since it passed through parliament.
Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri has a plan to solve the remaining 10 percent of the problems, he added.
The Interior Ministry said it had no information on the incident in Gerza on Thursday.
